scenes.headline: How one translator becomes four, on one base
scenes.sub: Text, speech, dubbing and long documents, post-trained from the same Qwen3.5 model.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Delphine! Index-Translate is one base model turned into four different translators. Here's how they share a spine.

scenes.text: One Qwen3.5 base becomes four translators: text, end-to-end speech, length-controlled dubbing, and whole-document translation. Same decoder underneath, four output interfaces.
scenes.say: The idea is one base, four post-trainings. The same text model becomes a speech translator, a dubbing model, and a long-document translator.

steps.say: Start with one Qwen base, at three sizes.
Mid-train it on one hundred and fifty languages.
Then post-train it four ways. Text translation. End-to-end speech.
Dubbing to a syllable budget. And whole documents in one pass.

scenes.title: Why dubbing needs a length dial

left.title: Plain translation
left.say: Translate a line faithfully and it can take far longer to say. The dub overruns the shot and lip-sync breaks.

right.title: Index-Homura
right.say: The dubbing head translates to a target syllable count, trained with a length reward, so the dubbed line fits the time the original took.

scenes.label: of dubs within 10% of the target syllable count
scenes.say: On the dubbing benchmark the nine B lands within ten percent of the target about eighty-two percent of the time.

scenes.title: FLORES COMET, same family and rivals
scenes.say: On the standard benchmark the nine B scores point eight seven eight nine, right at the front of the pack, and well above the base it came from.

scenes.text: One base, four jobs. The dubbing head hits the time budget, and the paper prints the quality it costs.
scenes.say: So: one base, four jobs. The dubbing head hits the time budget, and the paper is honest about the quality it costs.
One base, four translators. Text, speech, dubbing and long documents. All open weights.
